title: Magikarp Jump
statementMd:
Magikarp dreams of becoming a jumping champion and eventually evolving into a Gyarados! For now, he is practicing on a row of $n$ spots, numbered $1$ through $n$. The height of spot $i$ is $h_i$.

Magikarp starts at spot $1$ and wants to reach spot $n$. From spot $i$, he can jump to spot $i+1$, $i+2$, or $i+3$, as long as the destination does not exceed $n$. A jump from spot $i$ to spot $j$ costs $$ (h_i-h_j)^2 $$ energy. The total energy cost is the sum of the costs of all his jumps.

What is the minimum total energy cost for Magikarp to reach spot $n$?

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $n$ ($1 \le n \le 2\cdot 10^5$) — the number of spots.

The second line contains $n$ integers $h_1,h_2,\ldots,h_n$ ($0 \le h_i \le 10^6$) — the heights of the spots.

## Output

Output a single integer — the minimum total energy cost for Magikarp to reach spot $n$.

## Note

In the first sample, Magikarp can jump from spot $1$ to spot $3$, then to spot $6$. The total cost is $(10-20)^2+(20-20)^2=100$, which is the minimum possible.

In the second sample, one optimal route visits spots $1,4,6,7$, using jumps of lengths $3,2,1$. The total cost is $$ (0-0)^2+(0-1)^2+(1-10^6)^2=999998000002. $$

In the third sample, Magikarp can jump directly from spot $1$ to spot $4$. Both spots have height $1$, so the cost is $0$.

In the fourth sample, Magikarp is already at spot $n$, so he does not need to jump. The total cost is $0$.
